content: Individuals diagnosed with type 2 diabetes may need a combination of basal insulin and prandial (mealtime) insulin to effectively manage their blood glucose levels. A frequently utilized strategy involves incorporating a rapid-acting insulin, also known as bolus insulin, at mealtimes into an existing basal insulin regimen. The initial dosage of prandial insulin is typically calculated within the range of 0.1 to 0.5 units per kilogram of body weight per day. Dosage adjustments should be tailored to the specific needs of the patient, taking into account their target fasting blood glucose levels. Additionally, basal insulin therapy may be used in conjunction with other glucose-lowering medications to optimize glycemic control.
